summary: Obfuscated native-addon dropper executes encrypted payload on npm install
details: @testsecuiitytestme/cache-helper 1.0.7 ships a native Node addon at prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/node.napi.node accompanied by a 2.4MB high-entropy sibling file.napi_cache with no plaintext strings. The addon contains loader primitives (fork/execlp/setsid/chmod/CreateProcessA, format strings `%s/.napi_cache`, `/tmp/.%u`, `%s\.napi_cache`, `%s.nc%lu.js`, `node "%s"`) that decrypt the sibling blob, write it as a.js file into a per-user cache directory, and spawn `node` on it — an opaque loader-plus-encrypted-payload dropper. Execution is wired to npm install via package.json scripts.postinstall `patch-package || node index.js`: because patch-package is not declared as a dependency, the `||` fallback unconditionally runs `node index.js`, which require()s the native addon and triggers the dropper. The addon's string table also enumerates CI environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NOW_GITHUB_DEPLOYMENT, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER), container markers (/proc/1/cgroup, containerd, dockerinit, /proc/1/cmdline), debugger probes (TracerPid, IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, Process32First/Next, CreateToolhelp32Snapshot) and packet-sniffer process names (wireshark, httpdebug), consistent with environment-gated execution to evade analysis sandboxes. The package is published under the scope @testsecuiitytestme (misspelling of 'security'), reinforcing the delivery shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
